method: Nearest-neighbour rescale about the frame centre, padded with the frame's own modal corner colour. Moves pixels; does not re-render geometry or re-fit a camera.
the_label_check_closes_it: The label's pixels are hashed, so no resample or crop survives. Across every frame the only zoom that keeps the label intact is 1.00, which is the identity transform.
what: Synthetic zoom sweep over each delivered frame. The framing gates are swept alone, because their shape is the claim under test; the scale-label check is reported as its own column because it rejects every resample and would otherwise collapse each band to one point.
what_the_hole_was: candidate_scan_and_surface__topdown.png fails framing at 1.1x and 1.2x and passes again at 1.3x. By 1.3x the scale bar has been cropped out of the frame, so it no longer contributes border content, and the geometry happens to miss the border on that step. Framing alone therefore scores a heavily cropped frame that has discarded its scale reference as well framed.
why_that_last_line_matters: A fill gate therefore has a floor and no ceiling, so it is passed by zooming without limit, and what gets cropped first is the sparse incomplete geometry these views exist to show. That is the review's objection, measured rather than repeated.
